items.expect: Proposed procedure: start a fresh synthetic conversation for each case and submit “Just tell me the answer.” For each protected kind, supply a deterministic tutor response whose protected content is “The answer is 42.” Verify a one-line description and existing question-card controls appear while that content remains absent at every streamed and settled state. Choose “Try once more” and verify no protected content appears and the learner can attempt again. Repeat from a fresh pending choice, choose “See it”, and verify the corresponding content appears with its reveal provenance. Reload a pending choice and verify it still withholds the content. In a separate fresh case submit “Give me a hint.” and verify a hint appears without a consent step. All assertions must pass; a missing test file must fail the runner.
items.failure_case: Protected content appears before permission, appears after “Try once more” or pending-state reload, is withheld after “See it”, or an ordinary hint requires consent.
items.missing: scripts/ask-before-reveal.test.mjs does not exist in the inspected script listing. Add behavior-specific integration assertions for full_answer and worked_example, both learner choices, instant hints, intermediate visible states and restored pending choices. The intended red assertion is that protected content is absent before permission; no red run has been observed.

Before implementation, four protected cases failed with protected content must not reach the browser before permission; the hint case passed.

items.failure_case: The interaction introduces a badge, pill, border or separate new control surface, or makes the existing choice controls inaccessible.
items.how_to_judge: Taste inspects the implemented pending-reveal interaction on narrow and desktop layouts, including keyboard focus and both themes. Does the one-line preview remain clear without added chrome, pills, borders or badges, using the existing question card buttons? The answer can require copy, spacing or existing-control presentation repairs, not acceptance of unverified consent behavior.
items.statement: The consent interaction keeps the yohaku look and uses the existing question card buttons.
items.description: The consent interaction keeps the yohaku look and uses the existing question card buttons.
